Convert documents once. Give agents only what they need.

mcp-name: io.github.anishmoncivarghese/docsift

A 300-page PDF does not fit in a language model's context window, and pasting it in would be expensive if it did. DocSift converts documents into clean Markdown once, indexes them, and then hands back only the passages that answer a question — with page numbers and section headings, so the answer can be cited.

It runs on your machine. PDFs go through Docling, everything else through MarkItDown, both behind one interface. No cloud APIs, no accounts, no telemetry.

Where the saving comes from: retrieval, not conversion. Cleaning barely reduces tokens on PDFs, because Docling already strips headers and footers with its layout model. What changes the bill is asking a question and getting three relevant chunks back instead of a whole document.

Quickstart

Pick the engine you need — markitdown for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML, CSV and EPUB; docling for PDFs (a large download: ML layout models); all for both engines plus the HTTP API and MCP server.

pip install "docsift[markitdown]"
pip install "docsift[docling]"
pip install "docsift[all]"

docsift convert report.pdf

That writes cleaned Markdown, token-budgeted chunks and a JSON summary to ./output/. pip install docsift on its own installs the CLI but no engine, and conversion will tell you so rather than failing obscurely.

Use it from Claude, Codex, or another MCP client

The shortest path to the point of this tool: let an assistant search your own documents, without pasting them anywhere.

Which clients this works with

DocSift speaks MCP over stdio — the client starts it as a program on your machine. Anything that can do that is supported:

Client Supported How
Claude Code yes claude mcp add — step 2
Claude Desktop yes claude_desktop_config.json
VS Code (Copilot agent mode) yes .vscode/mcp.json
Codex CLI yes ~/.codex/config.toml
Cursor yes JSON config, same shape as VS Code
claude.ai in the browser no needs a remote server
ChatGPT (web or desktop) no needs a remote server

The last two are worth being clear about before you install anything. Their connector features only accept a remote MCP server at a public HTTPS URL, and DocSift has no remote transport — there is no configuration that makes a local one appear in those interfaces.

That is a deliberate position rather than an oversight. Reaching them means running DocSift on a server and uploading your documents to it, which is the opposite of the thing this tool is for. A self-hosted remote transport is a reasonable future addition; sending your files to someone else's machine is not.

1. Install it as a command, not into a project

An MCP client starts DocSift as a program, so it has to exist outside any virtualenv. Install it as a standalone tool:

uv tool install --python 3.12 "docsift[mcp,docling,markitdown]"

or with pipx:

pipx install --python python3.12 "docsift[mcp,docling,markitdown]"

DocSift needs Python 3.11 or newer. If your default is older, the version flag above is what avoids an unsatisfiable-requirements error. Expect a large download: docling brings PyTorch and layout models.

On Linux, add --torch-backend auto. The default resolves to the CUDA build of PyTorch — 5.3 GB installed, roughly 2 GB of it nvidia-* wheels that a machine without an NVIDIA GPU never loads. auto detects your driver and picks the right build, which is 1.6 GB on a machine without a GPU and leaves CUDA in place on one with a GPU:

uv tool install --python 3.12 --torch-backend auto "docsift[mcp,docling,markitdown]"

macOS wheels are CPU-only already, so the flag changes nothing there. It is a uv feature: with pipx or pip there is no equivalent, because the CPU builds live on a separate index and no published package can redirect an installer to it. If you install that way on a CPU-only Linux box, DocSift says so after your first conversion rather than letting several unused gigabytes pass unmentioned.

Check it landed. Run these one at a time; the second prints the path to the executable, which the next step needs.

docsift --version

which docsift

2. Register it with your client

Pick the one you use. You only need one of these.

Claude Code

$(which docsift) fills in the path for you, so this works exactly as written:

claude mcp add --scope user docsift -- "$(which docsift)" mcp

Then confirm it started — look for docsift ... ✔ Connected:

claude mcp list

--scope user makes it available in every project; without it, the server is registered only for the directory you were in.

That is the whole setup for Claude Code. Skip the other clients below and go to step 3.

VS Code

Copilot agent mode reads .vscode/mcp.json for one project, or the file behind the MCP: Open User Configuration command for all of them:

{
  "servers": {
    "docsift": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "/replace/with/the/path/from/which/docsift",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Codex CLI

~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.docsift]
command = "/replace/with/the/path/from/which/docsift"
args = ["mcp"]
startup_timeout_sec = 60

Raise the timeout as shown. Codex allows ten seconds by default and DocSift loads PyTorch on the way up, so the default reports a server that failed to start when it was only still starting.

Claude Desktop, Cursor

These read a JSON config file instead. For Claude Desktop on macOS that is ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json; create it if it does not exist.

If the file is empty or new, this is the whole contents — replacing the command with the path which docsift printed in step 1:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "docsift": {
      "command": "/replace/with/the/path/from/which/docsift",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

If it already has other servers, add docsift beside them rather than replacing the file — note the comma after the previous entry:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "something-you-already-had": {
      "command": "..."
    },
    "docsift": {
      "command": "/replace/with/the/path/from/which/docsift",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Use the absolute path, not a bare docsift. These clients do not reliably inherit your shell's PATH, and a wrong or bare path fails with ENOENT: no such file or directory.

Then restart the app — the config is read at startup.

Use the absolute path from which docsift, not a bare docsift. MCP clients do not reliably inherit your shell's PATH, and this is the most common reason a local server silently fails to start.

3. Ask

No commands to learn — describe what you want:

search ~/Documents/contract.pdf for the termination clause

what does report.pdf say about Q3 revenue?

The first question about a new file converts it, and on a PDF that is slow — about three minutes. That is startup cost, not page count: Docling downloads its layout and table models from HuggingFace on the very first conversion, then loads PyTorch. A three-page test file takes about as long as a thirty-page report, so picking something small to "try it quickly" does not help.

It happens once. Afterwards the file is recognised by its content and answers come back immediately, even if you move or rename it.

For a long PDF, convert it first and ask afterwards:

docsift convert big-report.pdf

That fills the same cache the MCP server reads, so the first question is as fast as the rest. It also sidesteps a real limit — MCP clients apply their own timeouts to a tool call, and a long enough conversion can exceed one and surface as an error even though it would have finished.

4. Check it works

Before pointing it at a real PDF, prove the wiring with a file that converts instantly. Make one:

printf '# Test\n\nDocSift returns only the passages that match a question.\n' > /tmp/docsift-check.md

Then ask your assistant, naming the tool:

use the docsift search_document tool on /tmp/docsift-check.md to search for "passages"

Name it explicitly, and watch which tool actually runs. Asked casually, an assistant will often just open a small file with its own file-reading tool and answer from that — you get the right answer having never touched DocSift, which makes a broken setup look like a working one. If your assistant reports reading a file rather than calling docsift, the check has told you nothing.

The first call will ask your permission to run the tool — approve it, and choose the "don't ask again" option if your client offers one, so later questions are not interrupted mid-thought.

Success looks like a docsift tool call in the transcript, returning that one sentence. This needs no PDF and no model weights, so a failure here is a setup problem — the command not on PATH, or the server not registered — and not a conversion one.

Then try a real PDF of your own, and expect the first question to take a minute. On a document of that size the choice takes care of itself: reading it whole is expensive, which is when searching it becomes the obvious move.

One test worth running deliberately: ask about something the document does not mention. You should get nothing back rather than a plausible-sounding answer. Search is lexical, so a word that is not in the text matches nothing — and seeing that once tells you more about what you can trust than a dozen successful queries.

What you get

Two tools:

  • search_document — the one that matters. Give it a file path and a question; it converts the file the first time it sees it, then returns only the passages that match, with page numbers and section headings.
  • convert_document — converts and indexes a file, returning a summary (page count, token estimate, chunk count) rather than the text.

What to expect

Measured on an Apple-silicon MacBook Air with a 34-page, 1.7 MB PDF — a BusinessEurope economic outlook, chosen because it is the awkward kind of document this tool exists for: dense tables, footnotes, multi-column stretches.
Whole document ~21,000 tokens, 42 chunks
One question answered ~4,000 tokens, 5 passages, with pages to cite
First conversion, ever ~3 minutes — mostly a one-time model download
First conversion of any later file seconds to a minute, by size
Every question after immediate

The token gap is the point, and it widens with document length.

Be clear about where the three minutes goes, because it is easy to misread as "big documents are slow". Most of it is Docling fetching its layout and table models the first time it ever runs, plus loading PyTorch. On a clean Linux machine a three-page, 1.8 KB PDF took 186 seconds — essentially the same as the 34-page report. After that first run the models are on disk and conversion scales with the document. docsift convert shows a live spinner throughout, so you can see it working rather than guessing.

search_document takes limit and max_tokens as well, and a model will set them when you ask for more or less. The defaults return five passages within a 5,000-token budget. Dense documents produce large chunks — around 1,000 tokens each in the report above — so if answers feel truncated, a larger max_tokens is the dial, and it is cheaper than the model asking the same question several times over.

One caveat the numbers do not show: search is lexical, not semantic. DocSift indexes chunks in SQLite FTS5 and ranks them with BM25. It matches the words you type — not synonyms, not paraphrases, not meaning. Ask for "termination clause" and a section that only ever says "ending the agreement" will not come back. Asking that report about "energy prices" surfaced a section on shipping and fertiliser costs because those passages happen to contain the phrase; a question worded "why did transport costs rise?" might have missed it entirely.

That is a deliberate trade, not an oversight: no embedding model to download, no index to rebuild, no GPU, nothing leaving your machine, and a first run measured in minutes rather than tens of minutes. If you need semantic retrieval, the Markdown and chunk JSON DocSift writes are clean input for a vector store — a reasonable thing to want, and not what this tool does today. See Known limitations.

Everything happens in that process, on your machine. Nothing listens on a port and no document content crosses the network. The server has exactly the filesystem access of the user who started it.

Not in the claude.ai connector directory, and it cannot be. claude.ai runs in the cloud and cannot start a program on your computer. A local MCP server works in apps running on your own machine — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor — and searching the web app's connector list for DocSift will never find it.

Command line

docsift convert report.pdf --max-tokens 800 --overlap 100
docsift convert report.pdf --engine markitdown
docsift inspect report.pdf
docsift compare report.pdf
docsift search doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx "operational risk"
docsift search doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx '"operational risk"' --limit 5 --context 1
docsift cache info
docsift cache clear

inspect reports what DocSift would do with a file — engine, identity, cache status — without converting it. compare runs both engines on the same document and writes a diff of the results.

Conversion cleans repeated headers and footers, page numbers and image references, then splits the text into token-budgeted chunks that carry their heading context. --keep-furniture and --keep-image-refs turn the cleaning stages off.

Results are cached, so an unchanged file with unchanged settings returns instantly. --no-cache forces a re-run.

Search is local SQLite FTS5 keyword ranking with quoted-phrase support. It reads the store the HTTP service and the MCP server write to — docsift convert writes standalone files to an output directory and does not add them to it. --context pulls in adjacent chunks, --max-tokens caps the whole response, and only selected chunks are ever printed. Scores order results within one response and are not comparable across requests.

HTTP API

pip install "docsift[all]"
docsift serve

Conversion always runs in the background: a long PDF can take minutes, and a client expecting a synchronous response will time out.

Upload, and get back 202 with a job id and a document id:

curl -sS -F file=@report.pdf http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/documents

Poll until the status is succeeded or failed:

curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/jobs/job_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

Then retrieve the whole document:

curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/documents/doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx/markdown
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/documents/doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx/chunks

Or ask a question and get only the relevant chunks:

curl -sS --get --data-urlencode 'q=operational risk' \
  --data 'limit=5' --data 'max_tokens=5000' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/documents/doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx/search

DELETE /v1/documents/{id} removes the document, its search index and its cached conversions — including cancelling a conversion still in flight, so a delete cannot be undone by a worker finishing afterwards. The OpenAPI document is at /openapi.json.

Set DOCSIFT_API_KEY before anything else can reach it. Every /v1/* route then requires an X-API-Key header, while /health, /version and the API docs stay open for health checks and connector imports. It is one shared secret for the whole service — not per-user identity, and no substitute for network controls. The service converts whatever it is given, so run it on infrastructure you control.

Power Platform, Copilot Studio and n8n

DOCSIFT_PUBLIC_URL=https://docsift.example docsift openapi --format swagger2 -o connector.json

Import that as a Power Platform custom connector. The service's own /openapi.json is OpenAPI 3.1, which custom connectors reject; this command emits the Swagger 2.0 they accept. Verified against a real tenant: the file imports, authenticates and returns schema-valid responses.

Worked examples live in examples/ — an importable n8n workflow, a Copilot Studio connector walkthrough, and the Power Automate Do until flow that waits for a conversion. A longer guide is in docs/USING_DOCSIFT.md.

More
Known limitations What DocSift does not do, stated plainly. Worth reading before you rely on it.
Configuration Every environment variable.
Docker Running the service in a container.
Deploying to Azure A hosted deployment, end to end.
Privacy What lands on disk, and the three times the network is touched.
Security The threat model, and how to report a vulnerability.
Contributing Setup, the gates, and what review looks for.
Changelog What shipped, and when.

License

MIT

content_html_zh:
转换文档一次。 只为代理提供他们需要的东西。

mcp 名称：io.github.anishmoncivarghese/docsift

300 页的 PDF 不适合语言模型的上下文窗口，如果适合的话，粘贴它的成本将会很高。 DocSift 将文档转换为干净的 Markdown 一次，对其进行索引，然后只返回回答问题的段落 - 带有页码和章节标题，以便可以引用答案。

它在您的机器上运行。 PDF 通过 Docling 处理，其他所有内容通过 MarkItDown 处理，两者都在同一个界面下进行。 没有云 API、没有帐户、没有遥测。

节省的来源：检索，而不是转换。 清理几乎不会减少 PDF 上的标记，因为 Docling 已经通过其布局模型去除了页眉和页脚。 该法案的改变在于提出一个问题并返回三个相关的块而不是整个文档。

快速入门

选择您需要的引擎 - Word、Excel、PowerPoint、HTML、CSV 和 EPUB 的 markitdown； PDF 文档（大量下载：ML 布局模型）；所有这些都适用于两个引擎以及 HTTP API 和 MCP 服务器。

pip install "docsift[markitdown]"
pip install "docsift[docling]"
pip install "docsift[all]"

docsift convert report.pdf

它将清理后的 Markdown、令牌预算块和 JSON 摘要写入 ./output/。 pip install docsift 本身会安装 CLI，但不会安装引擎，并且转换会告诉您这一点，而不是隐晦地失败。

从 Claude、Codex 或其他 MCP 客户端使用它

使用此工具的最短路径：让助手搜索您自己的文档，而无需将它们粘贴到任何地方。

适用于哪些客户

DocSift 通过 stdio 讲 MCP — 客户端将其作为计算机上的程序启动。 任何可以做到这一点的事情都受到支持：

客户 支持 How
克劳德·科德 yes 克劳德·MCP 添加 — 步骤 2
克劳德桌面 yes 克劳德桌面配置.json
VS Code（副驾驶代理模式） yes .vscode/mcp.json
法典 CLI yes 〜/.codex/config.toml
光标 yes JSON 配置，与 VS Code 的形状相同
浏览器中的 claude.ai no 需要一个远程服务器
ChatGPT（网络或桌面） no 需要一个远程服务器

在安装任何东西之前，最后两个值得弄清楚。 它们的连接器功能仅接受公共 HTTPS URL 上的远程 MCP 服务器，并且 DocSift 没有远程传输 - 没有任何配置可以使本地传输出现在这些界面中。

这是一个经过深思熟虑的立场，而不是疏忽。 达到这些目标意味着在服务器上运行 DocSift 并将文档上传到其中，这与该工具的用途相反。 自托管远程传输是未来合理的补充；将您的文件发送到其他人的计算机则不是。

1. 将其作为命令安装，而不是安装到项目中

MCP 客户端将 DocSift 作为程序启动，因此它必须存在于任何 virtualenv 之外。 将其作为独立工具安装：

uv tool install --python 3.12 "docsift[mcp,docling,markitdown]"

或使用 pipx：

pipx install --python python3.12 "docsift[mcp,docling,markitdown]"

DocSift 需要 Python 3.11 或更高版本。 如果您的默认版本较旧，则上面的版本标志可以避免出现无法满足要求的错误。 预计会有大量下载：docling 带来了 PyTorch 和布局模型。

在 Linux 上，添加 --torch-backend auto。 默认解析为 PyTorch 的 CUDA 版本 — 安装了 5.3 GB，其中大约 2 GB 的 nvidia-* 轮子是没有 NVIDIA GPU 的机器永远不会加载的。 auto 会检测您的驱动程序并选择正确的版本，在没有 GPU 的计算机上为 1.6 GB，并在有 GPU 的计算机上保留 CUDA：

uv tool install --python 3.12 --torch-backend auto "docsift[mcp,docling,markitdown]"

macOS 轮子已经仅支持 CPU，因此该标志不会改变任何内容。 这是一个 uv 功能：对于 pipx 或 pip 来说没有等效功能，因为 CPU 在单独的索引上实时构建，并且没有已发布的包可以将安装程序重定向到它。 如果您在仅使用 CPU 的 Linux 机器上以这种方式安装，DocSift 在您第一次转换后会这样说，而不是让几个未使用的千兆字节通过而未提及。

检查它是否落地。 一次运行这些；第二个打印下一步需要的可执行文件的路径。

docsift --version

which docsift

2. 向您的客户注册

选择您使用的那个。 您只需要其中之一。

克劳德·科德

$(which docsift) 会为您填写路径，因此其工作原理与所写的完全一样：

claude mcp add --scope user docsift -- "$(which docsift)" mcp

然后确认它已启动 - 查找 docsift ... ✔ 已连接：

claude mcp list

--scope user 使其在每个项目中都可用；如果没有它，服务器只会为您所在的目录注册。

这就是 Claude Code 的整个设置。 跳过下面的其他客户端并转到步骤 3。

VS代码

Copilot 代理模式读取一个项目的 .vscode/mcp.json，或 MCP 后面的文件：对所有项目打开用户配置命令：

{
  "servers": {
    "docsift": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "/replace/with/the/path/from/which/docsift",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

法典 CLI

〜/.codex/config.toml：

[mcp_servers.docsift]
command = "/replace/with/the/path/from/which/docsift"
args = ["mcp"]
startup_timeout_sec = 60

如图所示提高超时。 Codex 默认允许 10 秒，DocSift 在启动过程中加载 PyTorch，因此默认报告服务器在启动时无法启动。

克劳德桌面，光标

它们读取 JSON 配置文件。 对于 macOS 上的 Claude Desktop，路径为 ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json；如果不存在则创建它。

如果文件是空的或新的，这就是全部内容 - 将命令替换为 docsift 在步骤 1 中打印的路径：

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "docsift": {
      "command": "/replace/with/the/path/from/which/docsift",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

如果它已经有其他服务器，请在它们旁边添加 docsift 而不是替换文件 - 请注意上一个条目后面的逗号：

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "something-you-already-had": {
      "command": "..."
    },
    "docsift": {
      "command": "/replace/with/the/path/from/which/docsift",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

使用绝对路径，而不是裸露的 docsift。 这些客户端不能可靠地继承您的 shell 的 PATH，并且错误或裸路径会失败并显示 ENOENT: no such file or directory。

然后重新启动应用程序 - 配置在启动时读取。

使用 docsift 的绝对路径，而不是裸露的 docsift。 MCP 客户端无法可靠地继承 shell 的 PATH，这是本地服务器无提示启动失败的最常见原因。

3. Ask

无需学习命令——描述你想要什么：

搜索 ~/Documents/contract.pdf 查找终止条款
report.pdf 关于第三季度收入的情况如何？

关于新文件的第一个问题将其转换，并且在 PDF 上转换速度很慢 - 大约三分钟。 这是启动成本，而不是页数：Docling 在第一次转换时从 HuggingFace 下载其布局和表格模型，然后加载 PyTorch。 三页的测试文件大约需要三十页的报告一样长，因此选择一些小内容来“快速尝试”并没有帮助。

它发生一次。 之后，即使您移动或重命名文件，文件也会通过其内容进行识别，并且答案会立即返回。

对于较长的 PDF，请先将其转换，然后再询问：

docsift convert big-report.pdf

这会填充 MCP 服务器读取的相同缓存，因此第一个问题与其他问题一样快。 它还回避了一个真正的限制——MCP 客户端将自己的超时应用于工具调用，并且足够长的转换可能会超过 1，并显示为错误，即使它本来会完成。

4. 检查是否有效

在将其指向真正的 PDF 之前，请使用可立即转换的文件来验证连接。 制作一个：

printf '# Test\n\nDocSift returns only the passages that match a question.\n' > /tmp/docsift-check.md

然后询问你的助手，为该工具命名：

使用 /tmp/docsift-check.md 上的 docsift search_document 工具来搜索“passages”

明确命名它，并观察哪个工具实际运行。 随意询问时，助理通常会用自己的文件读取工具打开一个小文件，然后从中给出答案——你从未接触过 DocSift，就得到了正确的答案，这使得一个损坏的设置看起来像一个工作的设置。 如果您的助手报告正在读取文件而不是调用 docsift，则检查不会告诉您任何信息。

第一次通话将询问您运行该工具的许可 - 批准它，并选择“不再询问”选项（如果您的客户提供），这样后面的问题就不会被打断。

成功看起来就像在记录中调用 docsift 工具，返回那句话。 这不需要 PDF，也不需要模型权重，因此这里的失败是设置问题 - 命令不在 PATH 上，或者服务器未注册 - 而不是转换问题。

然后尝试您自己的真实 PDF，并预计第一个问题将花费一分钟时间。 对于这种大小的文档，选择是很自然的：阅读整个文档的成本很高，而当搜索它成为显而易见的举动时。

一项值得特意进行的测试：询问文档中未提及的内容。 除了听起来合理的答案之外，您应该什么也得不到。 搜索是基于词汇的，因此文本中没有的单词与任何内容都不匹配——并且一次看到它比十几个成功的查询更能告诉你什么是可以信任的。

你得到什么

两个工具：

  • search_document — 重要的那个。 给它一个文件路径和一个问题；它会在第一次看到文件时对其进行转换，然后仅返回匹配的段落以及页码和章节标题。
  • Convert_document — 转换并索引文件，返回摘要（页数、标记估计、块数）而不是文本。

会发生什么

在配备 34 页、1.7 MB PDF 的 Apple MacBook Air 上进行测量 — BusinessEurope 经济展望，选择此工具是因为它是一种尴尬的文档：密集的表格、脚注、多列延伸。
整个文件 约 21,000 个代币，42 个块
回答了一个问题 ~4,000 个标记，5 个段落，有可供引用的页面
有史以来第一次转换 约 3 分钟 — 大部分是一次性模型下载
任何后续文件的首次转换 秒到一分钟，按大小
之后的每个问题 即时

令牌间隙是关键，并且它随着文档长度的增加而变宽。

明确三分钟去哪儿了，因为很容易被误读为“大文档慢”。 其中大部分是 Docling 在第一次运行时获取其布局和表格模型，以及加载 PyTorch。 在一台干净的 Linux 机器上，一份 3 页、1.8 KB 的 PDF 需要 186 秒——与 34 页的报告基本相同。 第一次运行后，模型将存储在磁盘上，并且转换将随文档进行缩放。 docsift Convert 始终显示一个实时旋转器，因此您可以看到它正在工作，而不是猜测。

search_document 也接受 limit 和 max_tokens ，当您要求更多或更少时，模型会设置它们。 默认返回 5,000 代币预算内的 5 个段落。 密集的文档会产生大块（上面的报告中每个块大约有 1,000 个令牌），因此如果感觉答案被截断，可以使用更大的 max_tokens 来进行调整，并且它比多次询问同一问题的模型要便宜。

数字没有显示一个警告：搜索是词汇的，而不是语义的。 DocSift 对 SQLite FTS5 中的块进行索引，并使用 BM25 对它们进行排名。 它与您输入的单词相匹配 - 不是同义词，不是释义，不是含义。 要求“终止条款”，而只说“终止协议”的部分将不会出现。 询问该报告有关“能源价格”的内容时，出现了有关运输和化肥成本的部分，因为这些段落恰好包含这个短语；一个措辞为“为什么运输成本上涨？”的问题 可能完全错过了。

这是一种深思熟虑的交易，而不是疏忽：无需下载嵌入模型，无需重建索引，没有 GPU，没有任何东西离开您的机器，并且首次运行以分钟而不是数十分钟为单位。 如果您需要语义检索，Markdown 和块 JSON DocSift 写入是矢量存储的干净输入 - 一个合理的需求，而不是这个工具现在所做的事情。 请参阅已知限制。

一切都发生在这个过程中，在您的机器上。 端口上没有任何内容侦听，也没有文档内容通过网络。 服务器完全具有启动它的用户的文件系统访问权限。

不在 claude.ai 连接器目录中，也不可能在。 claude.ai 在云端运行，无法在您的计算机上启动程序。 本地 MCP 服务器在您自己的计算机上运行的应用程序中工作 - Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Codex、Cursor - 在 Web 应用程序的连接器列表中搜索 DocSift 将永远找不到它。

命令行

docsift convert report.pdf --max-tokens 800 --overlap 100
docsift convert report.pdf --engine markitdown
docsift inspect report.pdf
docsift compare report.pdf
docsift search doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx "operational risk"
docsift search doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx '"operational risk"' --limit 5 --context 1
docsift cache info
docsift cache clear

Inspect 报告 DocSift 将如何处理文件——引擎、身份、缓存状态——而不转换它。 比较在同一个文档上运行两个引擎并写入结果的差异。

转换会清除重复的页眉和页脚、页码和图像引用，然后将文本拆分为带有标题上下文的标记预算块。 --keep-furniture 和 --keep-image-refs 关闭清洁阶段。

结果被缓存，因此设置未更改的未更改文件会立即返回。 --no-cache 强制重新运行。

搜索是本地 SQLite FTS5 关键字排名，支持引用短语。 它读取 HTTP 服务和 MCP 服务器写入的存储 — docsift Convert 将独立文件写入输出目录，但不会将它们添加到其中。 --context 拉入相邻的块， --max-tokens 限制整个响应，并且只打印选定的块。 对一个响应中的订单结果进行评分，并且跨请求之间不可比较。

HTTP API

pip install "docsift[all]"
docsift serve

转换始终在后台运行：较长的 PDF 可能需要几分钟的时间，并且期望同步响应的客户端将会超时。

上传，并返回 202 以及作业 id 和文档 id：

curl -sS -F file=@report.pdf http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/documents

轮询直到状态成功或失败：

curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/jobs/job_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

然后检索整个文档：

curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/documents/doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx/markdown
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/documents/doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx/chunks

或者提出一个问题并仅获取相关的块：

curl -sS --get --data-urlencode 'q=operational risk' \
  --data 'limit=5' --data 'max_tokens=5000' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/documents/doc_xxxxxxxxxxxx/search

DELETE /v1/documents/{id} 会删除文档、其搜索索引及其缓存的转换，包括取消仍在进行中的转换，因此之后完成的工作人员无法撤消删除操作。 OpenAPI 文档位于 /openapi.json。

在其他任何东西到达之前设置 DOCSIFT_API_KEY。 每个 /v1/* 路由都需要一个 X-API-Key 标头，而 /health、/version 和 API 文档保持开放状态以进行运行状况检查和连接器导入。 它是整个服务的一个共享秘密——不是每个用户的身份，也不能替代网络控制。 该服务会转换给定的任何内容，因此在您控制的基础设施上运行它。

Power Platform、Copilot Studio 和 n8n

DOCSIFT_PUBLIC_URL=https://docsift.example docsift openapi --format swagger2 -o connector.json

将其导入为 Power Platform 自定义连接器。 该服务自己的 /openapi.json 是 OpenAPI 3.1，自定义连接器会拒绝该版本；该命令发出他们接受的 Swagger 2.0。 针对真实租户进行验证：文件导入、验证并返回架构有效的响应。

工作示例位于示例/中 - 可导入的 n8n 工作流程、Copilot Studio 连接器演练以及等待转换的 Power Automate Do Until 流程。 更长的指南位于 docs/USING_DOCSIFT.md 中。
